title: Irreducible component closures and dimensions in an arbitrary blowup
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $q:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be of finite type, with $X$ reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $I$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf with support $C\subseteq X$, put $X'=I.\mathrm{strictTransform}(\mathrm{id}_X)$, and write $\pi:X'\to X$ for its projection [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-strict-transform]. For each irreducible component $W$ of $X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] put $T(W)=\overline{\pi^{-1}(W\setminus C)}$. Then $V\subseteq X'$ is an irreducible component if and only if $V=T(W)$ for some irreducible component $W\subseteq X$ with $W\setminus C\ne\varnothing$. For every such $W$ one has $\dim T(W)=\dim W$, with topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. No component-avoidance hypothesis on the centre, smoothness, characteristic-zero assumption, or Hilbert--Samuel equality is imposed.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes X Noetherian with finitely many components. Its affine centre ideals are finitely generated. The blowup is proper, hence finite type. Identify its strict-transform presentation with the intrinsic blowup.

The scheme-theoretic strict transform is the closure of its preserved open, whose projection is isomorphic to U = X minus the centre. The preserved open is reduced, so its schematic closure is reduced and has the topological closure as its support. Each component W meeting U gives the irreducible closure of the lifted W intersect U. These finitely many closures cover, and none contains another: restricting a containment to the preserved open gives containment of distinct components of U. Thus W-prime is a component upstairs if and only if it is one of the asserted closures, with W minus the centre nonempty.

Give W and its surviving closure the reduced induced closed subscheme structures. Both are integral and locally finite type over the field. Their nonempty unchanged opens are isomorphic, hence their function fields agree over the field. Compute the dimension on a nonempty affine open using finiteType_domain_ringKrullDim_eq_trdeg, and use equality of dimension with a nonempty open for integral locally algebraic schemes. The two dimensions are equal.
